sections.title: A counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture
sections.abstract: The paper constructs a division-ring extension yielding a triangular ring that is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type, contradicting the pure semisimplicity conjecture.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete counterexample to a long-standing conjecture, an accompanying Lean 4 formalization linked from the arXiv comments, and early external coverage by MathWorld and AI Proof Watch. These are attention/checkability signals, not peer review.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that the triangular ring built from the specified division-ring extension is right pure semisimple, but not left pure semisimple and not of finite representation type; this would refute the conjecture.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The construction uses a division ring T formed from fraction division rings of nearest-neighbour quantum Laurent algebras with parameter 1/2, and a subring H with right dimension sequence (1,2,2,…).
sections.unique_caveat: This is a preprint claim. The arXiv comment says the Lean development corresponds to an earlier manuscript snapshot, so it does not alone certify the current version.
sections.comment: 10 pages; Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem linked; author invites comments and corrections.

sections.title: A proof of the Murty--Simon conjecture on diameter-2-critical graphs
sections.abstract: The authors prove that every finite n-vertex diameter-2-critical graph has at most floor(n²/4) edges, with equality only for the balanced complete bipartite graph, for every n.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The claimed result closes the all-n conjecture, including its equality case; a public Lean 4/Mathlib formalization was independently located and checked. This is a theorem-and-verifiability basis for placement, not a citation-based popularity signal.
sections.claimed_result: The paper proves the Murty--Simon edge bound and uniqueness of the extremal graph for every n≥3; its introduction reduces the proof to a maximal-matching inequality and a characterization of equality.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite diameter-2-critical graphs: every vertex pair is at distance at most 2, and deleting any edge destroys that property.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that AI first found the edge-bound proof; they simplified it and developed the equality-case argument themselves. This remains a preprint claim requiring mathematical review.

sections.title: Nonuniqueness of the 2D Euler Evolutions with L¹∩Lᵖ Vorticity
sections.abstract: For each fixed 1<p<∞, the authors construct one compactly supported initial vorticity in L¹∩Lᵖ that has two distinct, exactly transported evolutions of the unforced planar Euler equation on [0,1].
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The introduction states a precise theorem for every finite p, with both evolutions strongly continuous in the stated norms and transported by regular Lagrangian flows. The authors also identify a contemporaneous independent construction using essentially the same core mechanism.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove nonuniqueness by coupling unstable four-vortex configurations across infinitely many scales so a vanishing initial perturbation leaves a detectable difference at positive time.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Unforced two-dimensional incompressible Euler; the datum is real and compactly supported, and may depend on the prescribed finite exponent p. Each flow is almost-everywhere invertible and measure-preserving.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction does not claim nonuniqueness at p=∞; the authors distinguish finite-Lᵖ membership from stronger quantitative control as p grows. They also cite Choi's independently developed work using essentially the same mechanism.

sections.title: JT gravity as a conformal scaling limit of random flat combinatorial disks
sections.abstract: The paper proves a criterion based on branching explorations and applies it to a Boltzmann ensemble of rectilinear-boundary combinatorial disks, whose rescaled surfaces converge to the continuum random surface prescribed by flat JT gravity.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in probability and mathematical physics; the abstract states a scaling-limit theorem and a branching-exploration criterion, with a conformal-welding theorem supplied by a companion paper. Semantic Scholar reports 0 citations at the snapshot; that is a current total, not a period gain.
sections.claimed_result: As a distinguished boundary side tends to infinite length, the rescaled disk converges in law, in the stated interior conformal-factor topology, to the flat JT-gravity surface; under a tightness condition the criterion extends to discrete disks.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The worked example is a Boltzmann ensemble of disks with rectilinear boundary; the limit uses uniformization in a fixed domain and a branching exploration with conditioned Cauchy-process lengths.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is established for the stated ensemble and criterion; other natural disk models are proposed as applications, not proved scaling limits here.

sections.title: An Adian-Rabin theorem for quantum automorphism groups of graphs
sections.abstract: The authors prove that many properties of graph quantum-automorphism groups—including having quantum symmetries and having a nontrivial discrete quantum automorphism group—are undecidable.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It is cross-listed across four mathematical subjects and gives explicit undecidability results; Semantic Scholar currently lists 1 citation and 0 influential citations, a current total rather than a period gain.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish an Adian-Rabin theorem for quantum automorphism groups of graphs and for solution groups associated with linear-system nonlocal games.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The objects are graph quantum-automorphism algebras and their discrete quantum groups; the method reduces questions to solution groups of linear-system games.
sections.unique_caveat: Undecidability rules out a general decision procedure but does not classify the quantum symmetries of any particular graph.

sections.title: Serre's conjectures for Q(√13)
sections.abstract: Assuming GRH and a minor technical result, the authors claim to prove Serre's conjectures for Q(√13) and establish a reduction-to-level-1 result for real quadratic fields with narrow class number one.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract combines a named conjecture for a specific field with a reduction theorem over a broader class of real quadratic fields; the result is explicitly conditional rather than an unconditional resolution.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the conjectures for Q(√13) under the stated assumptions and a reduction-to-level-1 theorem for every real quadratic field of narrow class number one.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: GRH and one minor technical result are assumed; the field-specific base cases are established only for Q(√13).
sections.unique_caveat: The argument is conditional, and the authors say they cannot yet establish the needed base cases for other fields.

sections.title: A complete solution to the reverse isoperimetric problem for λ-convex bodies
sections.abstract: For λ>0, the authors show that among λ-convex bodies in Euclidean space with fixed surface area, the intersection of two radius-1/λ balls minimizes volume, confirming Borisenko's conjecture in every dimension n≥2.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract claims a complete all-dimensions resolution and extends the inequality to all constant-curvature model spaces; cross-listed in metric and differential geometry.
sections.claimed_result: The λ-convex lens minimizes volume at fixed surface area in Rⁿ, and the authors extend the reverse inequality to constant-curvature model spaces in arbitrary dimension and for every λ>0.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: λ-convex means an intersection of balls of radius 1/λ; λ is positive and surface area is fixed.
sections.unique_caveat: The result concerns this constrained class and the stated constant-curvature model spaces, not arbitrary convex bodies in arbitrary ambient geometries.

sections.title: A self-normalized law of the iterated logarithm for Rademacher random multiplicative functions
sections.abstract: For a squarefree-supported Rademacher random multiplicative function, the authors prove a two-sided law of the iterated logarithm normalized by its full predictable quadratic variation, with almost-sure cluster set [-1,1].
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A precise almost-sure limit theorem and an explicit probability/number-theory bridge; the abstract also isolates a remaining growth dichotomy rather than claiming it is settled.
sections.claimed_result: The normalized partial sums have limsup 1, liminf -1, and cluster set [-1,1]; moreover, no positive deterministic q makes Q(x)/q(x) converge in probability to 1.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: f is a Rademacher random multiplicative function supported on squarefree integers, and Q is the full predictable quadratic variation of the prime-revealing martingale.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors do not decide whether a second limsup, normalized by √x(log log x)^(1/4), is finite and positive with a nondegenerate law or infinite almost surely.

sections.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperkähler Manifolds
sections.abstract: The author proves that every compact hyperkähler manifold is bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojević and Stelzig, using algebraic formality results for multicomplexes and commutative n-differential graded algebras.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across algebraic topology, algebraic geometry, and differential geometry; the abstract states a general algebraic theorem and a geometric application. No citation or independent discussion signal was available in the sources checked.
sections.claimed_result: The author establishes a generalized ∂∂̄-lemma and an algebraic formality theorem for the stated multicomplex setting, yielding strong formality for compact hyperkähler manifolds.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The geometric conclusion is for compact hyperkähler manifolds; the algebraic framework is categories of multicomplexes and commutative n-differential graded algebras.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not claim the same conclusion for broader classes of non-Kähler manifolds.
